Below is a quick analysis of what’s going on and a minimal set of edits to get your G-code highlighter picked up correctly.

### What’s happening?  
Prism’s demo harness (in `components/index.js`) takes each key of `components.languages` (“language”) and builds a path like:  
```js
var pathToLanguage = './prism-' + language;
```
If you’ve named your grammar file `prism-reprap-gcode.js` (with a dash) but your language ID in `components.languages` is `reprap_gcode` (with an underscore) it will look for `prism-reprap_gcode.js` instead and never find it.

By normalizing underscores → dashes when building the require path, Prism will correctly load your file.

---

```javascript
### components/index.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
			var pathToLanguage = './prism-' + language;
=======
			// normalize underscores to dashes so that
			// reprap_gcode → prism-reprap-gcode.js
			var pathToLanguage = './prism-' + language.replace(/_/g, '-');
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With that one small tweak, when you add your G-code component under `components.languages` as e.g.:

```js
// in components.js (not shown above)
...
reprap_gcode: {
  title: 'G-code',
  require: [],
  alias: ['gcode'],
  path: 'components/prism-reprap-gcode.js',
  examplesPath: 'examples/prism-reprap-gcode.html'
},
...
```

the loader will look for `./prism-reprap-gcode.js` (dash) instead of `./prism-reprap_gcode.js` (underscore) and your highlighter will get registered.
